ground_truth.description: The positional arguments to_sha and from_sha are swapped in the git diff command. The original order was 'from_sha, to_sha' but the new code passes 'to_sha, from_sha', which reverses the diff direction. This produces the inverse of the intended changeset — additions appear as deletions and vice versa.
The --diff-filter flag excludes Type-change (T) files by default. While rare, symlink-to-file type changes would be silently dropped from the results.

task.title: Add include_deleted to GitOps.get_changed_files and a shortstat diff-stats helper
task.description: `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py::GitOps.get_changed_files` hands callers every path git reports between two commits, with no way to say whether deletions belong in the answer: rollback validation needs the removed paths, while today's callers want only the files that still exist after the change. Add an `include_deleted: bool = False` parameter that selects the diff filter accordingly, where the default may narrow the result to paths that still exist after the change. Add a sibling `GitOps.get_diff_stats(from_sha, to_sha)` returning `{'insertions': N, 'deletions': N}` parsed from `git diff --shortstat`, so callers can size a changeset without shelling out themselves. Both stay on the module's existing `_run` helper with `cwd=self.project_root`.
task.test_strategy: Extend `orchestrator/tests/test_git_ops.py` with a temporary repo whose second commit adds, modifies and deletes files: assert `get_changed_files` returns the expected path set over that commit range with `include_deleted` both False and True, and that `get_diff_stats` matches the insertion/deletion counts git itself reports for the same range.
